title: Marketplace orders visible to the buyer and to the sellers of any item
issue: An order is visible to its buyer OR to any staff member of a seller whose product is in the order (order_items -> products -> sellers). The policy needs an OR across two derivations, one of them a three-table join; policies cannot read the RLS-protected order_items from the orders policy (42P17), so it is wrapped in security definer helpers that run per row or build a big id array. order_items and shipments inherit the order's visibility.
symptom: naive_rls (per-row security definer helper doing a 3-table join) is orders of magnitude slower for sellers; best_practice_rls (InitPlan array of the seller's order ids) pays to build the array per query and cannot use it for joins/aggregates cheaply. pg_auth models the order once (buyer, seller-from-items) and pays in tuples: one buyer tuple per order and one item_seller tuple per (order, seller).

scale.meaning: number of orders (3 items each, shipments for ~60%). buyers = scale/5, sellers = scale/300 (seller 1 owns ~10% of all products and is in ~27% of all orders), products = scale/10. At 10x (300k orders): 900k items, 3k sellers, 30k products, ~180k shipments; OpenFGA tuples are ~ 300k buyer + ~800k item_seller + ~3k staff = ~1.1M, i.e. they grow with orders (the order object is modelled per order), unlike the membership-level scenarios. Generated with generate_series inserts only.
